name: Real-world run (the “What the Ice Kept” log)

parts.name: one AI times out on every call of one kind while two others work
parts.about: The log's ChatGPT: the reply could not be read, so every request of that kind timed out (typed, no answer, late window expired). Claude and Gemini answered everything. Does the step move to a working AI, or stop the book — and how long does the run wait?

parts.name: an answer that arrives late
parts.about: The prompt was typed, the answer came after the timeout: inside the late-answer window (is it used?) or only after LATE_EXPIRED (is it thrown away, and what does asking again cost?).

parts.name: every AI times out
parts.about: No AI can answer: the expected result is a safe stop (🟡) — how long before it?

parts.name: a stop while the author is away
parts.about: The run stopped on a TIMEOUT at night. How long until anything happens on its own (no auto-retry, the stand-in vote off by default)?

parts.name: the finished book without a pen name
parts.about: No pen name was typed: what do the title page, the running heads and the metadata of the PDF / EPUB / DOCX say?

parts.name: a long sentence repeated across chapters
parts.about: The same long sentence word for word in chapters 1 and 3: does any check catch it, and is it still in the finished book?

parts.name: a book over its length target and the cut pass
parts.about: Chapters written well over their share: does the cut pass keep any of the editor's cuts?

parts.name: the editor reads a version that is not the final one
parts.about: After the editor's read the chapter changes again (planned details, cuts, the opening pass): which version did the editor's notes describe?

parts.name: planned details missing from the page at the end
parts.about: The planned-to-page check keeps finding the same planned details missing and the rewrites do not add them: what does the finished book / the author get?

parts.name: out of the box: more from the log
parts.about: The writer's AI pane broken for hours, the bridge reporting the stalled AI, ChatGPT failing every kind for the whole night with the author pressing Try again, and the clean-run score.

results.title: ChatGPT times out on every review call while the two other AIs work
results.happened: ChatGPT timed out on every review call (typed, no answer, late window expired); the two other AIs worked. The run stopped 4× (TIMEOUT@canon, TIMEOUT@chapters, TIMEOUT@chapters, TIMEOUT@chapters); the author pressed 🔁 Try again each time, then the fault was removed. results.problem_fix: The AI did not answer in time. Akọwe already waited for a late answer and asked another AI (or the same one again), so it stopped here instead of guessing. finding.where: akowe/akowe/assist.py `_call_ai_once` (~line 695–745): the checker jobs (review, scenes_check, editor, planned_check, writers' room …) pick a slot themselves and call `prov.generate(..., slot_id=slot["slot_id"])` (line ~720); in akowe/akowe/providers.py `_generate` (~1590–1660) an explicit slot_id means `others=False` (line ~1637), so `_generate_timeout_safe` (~1688) asks the SAME web AI once more after TIMEOUT_RETRY_WAIT_S (60 s) instead of moving; back in assist the failover branch (line ~733) moves only on UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE / AI_DECLINED / unusable — `_unusable` explicitly excludes TIMEOUT — so the TIMEOUT is raised
finding.cause: TIMEOUT is treated as “ambiguous, the author decides” (contract rule from the paid-API days), but a web AI whose prompt was typed and whose late window expired (`late_expired` / `late_collect_tried`) is not ambiguous any more: nothing more will come. Each such call costs the full timeout (~895 s: `AutoInjectorAdapter.timeout_ms` caps at 900 s) + the late window (300 s) + 60 s + the same again on the -c1- try ≈ 41 min, then the checker stops the book or is skipped. The failed-slot hold (FAIL_HOLD_S = 15 s) is long over by the next call, so the next call of the same kind goes to the same AI again
finding.fix: in assist `_call_ai_once`, treat a TIMEOUT whose bridge body says typed + late_expired (or late_collect_tried) like UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE: add the slot to `failed` and move to another working AI (`_other_ai`), keeping the writer≠reviewer rule; do not do the 60 s same-AI retry when another AI could take the call; mark the slot failed for much longer than 15 s after a TIMEOUT (e.g. until its next successful probe), so the next call of any kind starts elsewhere
finding.what: review: 4 stops while Claude and Gemini worked, ≈ 4.8 h lost (the log's review ×4)

finding.where: akowe/akowe/providers.py `_generate` / `_generate_timeout_safe` (~1590–1710): the registry path (no slot_id) DOES move a TIMEOUT to the next working AI, but only after the whole timeout + late window (~20 min for a 900 s deadline, ~11 min for the writer's 355 s), and the bible batch got the 60 s same-AI retry first (book_bible fill → ~41 min, then BIBLE_FILL_LATER)
finding.cause: there is no early signal: Akọwe waits the full timeout it asked for, then the late window; the failed-slot hold is 15 s, so each new chapter starts on the AI that timed out again (3 chapters → 3 full timeouts)
finding.fix: after a TIMEOUT with late_expired, keep the slot “failed” until a probe says it answers again (not 15 s); give the writer's later chapters to the AI that took over; shorten timeout_ms when the bridge reports a stalled capture (see R-10-c)
finding.what: bible fill: ≈ 41 min on the same AI, then a batch left for later

results.title: the reviewer's answer arrives only after LATE_EXPIRED (too late)
results.happened: ChatGPT's first review answer came only after the late window had closed (LATE_EXPIRED): it was thrown away (Akọwe forgets the late request; AutoInjector drops a reply after LATE_EXPIRED), and the same prompt was typed AGAIN into ChatGPT's chat (the -c1- try) 20.9 min after the first send; that answer was used; the run never stopped.
risks: the second try went to the SAME AI (ChatGPT, -c1-) after a 60 s wait, typing the whole prompt again into a chat that already holds the late answer, while Gemini and Claude were free
the run waited ≈ 20.9 min on the AI that could not answer before anything moved (limit 5.0 min when another AI works)
notes: Measured: status done; 0 stop(s); time waited ≈ 20.9 min (simulated clock); 1 TIMEOUT / 1 LATE_EXPIRED / 0 late answer(s) used; answered in the end by ChatGPT, Gemini.

finding.where: akowe/akowe/providers.py `_generate_timeout_safe` (~1688–1710) and `_post_collecting` (~1100): after LATE_EXPIRED the late request is forgotten (`_forget_late`) and, with an explicit slot, the whole prompt is sent again to the SAME AI after 60 s (bridge id -c1-)
finding.cause: the answer that arrives after LATE_EXPIRED is dropped by AutoInjector and Akọwe has no way to ask for it; the second try is a new prompt typed into the chat that already holds the late answer
finding.fix: move the second try to another working AI when one exists (see R-1); optionally ask AutoInjector for a reply that arrived after LATE_EXPIRED under the old request id before typing again
finding.what: a late answer after LATE_EXPIRED is thrown away and the same AI is asked again: ≈ 21 min
